ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The magnetic induction intensity of the uniform magnetic field is $B=0.1\mathrm{T}$, the number of turns of the rectangular coil used is $n=100$, the side lengths are $l_{AB}=0.2\mathrm{m}$ and $l_{BC}=0.5\mathrm{m}$, and it rotates uniformly around the symmetry axis $OO^{\prime}$ with an angular velocity $\omega=100\pi\mathrm{rad/s}$. Timing starts when the coil plane passes through the neutral plane.

1. What is the magnitude of the induced electromotive force in the coil?
2. What is the average electromotive force during the process from $t=0$ to $t=\frac{T}{4}$?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The magnetic induction intensity of the uniform magnetic field is $B=0.1\mathrm{T}$, the number of turns of the rectangular coil used is $n=100$, the side lengths are $l_{AB}=0.2\mathrm{m}$ and $l_{BC}=0.5\mathrm{m}$, and it rotates uniformly around the symmetry axis $OO^{\prime}$ with an angular velocity $\omega=100\pi\mathrm{rad/s}$. Timing starts when the coil plane passes through the neutral plane. 1. What is the magnitude of the induced electromotive force in the coil? 2. What is the average electromotive force during the process from $t=0$ to $t=\frac{T}{4}$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coil ABCD, with A and B on the left side and D and C on the right side; multiple horizontal rightward arrows represent a uniform magnetic field; the dashed line OO′ passes through the center of the coil, indicating that the coil rotates around this axis of symmetry, and the angular velocity ω is also marked in the figure. Reasoning: The area of the rectangular coil S = l_AB·l_BC = 0.2×0.5 = 0.1 m². Timing starts when the plane of the coil passes through the neutral plane; at this time the magnetic flux is maximum, so the total flux linkage can be written as nΦ = nBS cos(ωt). The magnitude of the induced electromotive force is e = |d(nΦ)/dt|, and according to the phase expression set by the problem, e(t)=nBSω sin(ωt). Substituting B=0.1 T, n=100, S=0.1 m², ω=100π rad/s, the maximum value E_m = 100×0.1×0.1×100π = 100π ≈ 314 V, therefore e(t)=314 sin(100πt) V. From t=0 to t=T/4, the flux linkage changes from nBS to 0, and the magnitude of the change is nBS. Also T=2π/ω, so T/4=π/(2ω). The magnitude of the average electromotive force is E_avg = nBS/(T/4)=2nBSω/π = 2×100×0.1×0.1×100π/π = 200 V.
